decision: Use a bounded process-per-call qrexec-client-vm invoker as the real-Qubes Phase-1 adapter feeding the existing read-only qualification collector.

comparison.correctness: Directly exercises the documented VM-to-VM qrexec path and preserves the real process exit code, response bytes, and frame count consumed by qualification.
comparison.robustnessSecurity: No shell, fixed argv separation, bounded stdout, timeout kill, ignored stderr, and no MissionQueue mutation API. Denials remain non-zero observations; transport faults fail closed.
comparison.latency: One qrexec process per scenario with no added protocol round trip beyond the qualification invocation itself.
comparison.resourceUse: No daemon, database, WAL, or persistent transport state; bounded response buffering and bounded wall-clock duration.
comparison.regressionRisk: Isolated adapter with dependency-injected spawn implementation; existing collector and protocol semantics are unchanged.
comparison.qa: Unit coverage checks argv/shell isolation, allowed JSON framing, policy-denial observation, output-bound kill, missing scenario rejection, and sanitized spawn failure handling. Real-Qubes execution remains a separate acceptance gate.

rejected.reason: Adds lifecycle, IPC, memory, and cross-request state without improving Phase-1 evidence.
Introduces quoting/injection risk and unnecessary shell semantics.
Mixes policy/routing failures with MissionQueue behavior and increases blast radius before read-only routing is proven.

failuresLessons: Node-level collector tests cannot prove Qubes policy routing; the adapter must invoke qrexec-client-vm on a real Worker Qube.
Remote stderr should not become qualification evidence because it can contain paths or diagnostic material; exit status and bounded stdout are sufficient for this gate.
Coordinator-side before/after MissionStore and RequestJournal digests remain mandatory and are intentionally supplied independently to the collector.
safety: Read-only synthetic qualification only; no financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflows, or weakened controls.
